bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating cultural relevance through automatic detection of culturally specific lexical items, named entities, and idiomatic expressions, combined with cross-linguistic/multilingual embedding similarity measures, and structured human assessments of inclusivity and absence of culturally alienating content.

Assessing the accessibility of simplified texts for individuals with lower health literacy and education levels using automatic readability indices (e.g., FKGL, SMOG), cohesion tools, pragmatic feature extraction, and human comprehension surveys to prevent communication disparities.
Measuring clarity, tone, and trustworthiness across different dialects and user demographics to ensure text simplification does not over-index on English-dominant, highly educated populations.
